newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks seen unmoved by election violence.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks seen unmoved by election violence.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks were seen flat ahead of next month's local government polls and the market was not likely to be affected by the murder of a parliament deputy of the ruling coalition, brokers said.
"(The shooting) is definitely not a good sign, but we don't think it alone will have a major impact on the market," said Sanjeeva Gunewardena, manager institutional sales at Commercial Stock Brokers.
Unknown assailants shot dead lawmaker Nalanda Ellawela from the ruling People's Alliance a day before nominations for the polls were due to close.

"Foreign investors would take note of this, but they are not very active at this moment," said Namal Kamalgoda, fund manager equities at CTC Eagle Fund Management. "Local investors will generally discount this kind of information."
But the market was expected to remain flat until after the election, tentatively scheduled for March 27, Kamalgoda said. On Tuesday, the all share index closed 1.03 points lower at 620.86.
